solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fat swine blocks old port

indicators.note: to block something is to sit in its way, so one piece is lodged in the middle of another

blocks.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A fat pig is stuck in the way at a harbour that has seen better days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old port' looks like a harbour town, but it is the ship's left-hand side, and the pig sits inside the fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Larboard was the former seafaring term for the left side of a ship, later replaced by port to avoid confusion with starboard.

clue.text: Clout Victor inside shelter with Vogue

indicators.note: something inside is held within the walls of another piece

blocks.note: Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
a rage is a craze or fashion, as in 'all the rage'

explanation.surface: Someone with power hits back, sheltering alongside a famous fashion magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Vogue is not the magazine but a passing fashion, as in 'all the rage'; the lee is the side sheltered from the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Clout and leverage both mean influence or power used to get results, typically in business or politics.

clue.text: Concern of EV buyers published outside of garage

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its two end letters, leaving the middle behind

blocks.note: a newspaper ran a story when it published it
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: An article appears about a car dealership's electric-vehicle customers and what worries them.
explanation.walkthrough: EV is short for electric vehicle; buyers worry how far one travels between charges.
explanation.definitionFit: The distance an electric car can drive on a full battery is a well-known worry for prospective owners, termed range anxiety.

clue.text: Taxing forums alternately visited by emperor

indicators.note: taking every other letter means using one, skipping one, all the way along
a visitor steps inside the home of whoever is visited, so one piece enters another

blocks.note: second, fourth and sixth letters
Nero was a Roman emperor

explanation.surface: An emperor drops in on public meetings every other day, which is a burden for all.
explanation.walkthrough: Nero goes between the O and the US taken from the forums.
explanation.definitionFit: Something onerous is heavy and demanding, just as a taxing job strains your energy and patience.

clue.text: Heartless competitor Omani bit

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter is cut out

blocks.note: a rival is a competitor

explanation.surface: A ruthless opponent from Oman makes a cutting remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit' looks like a verb about biting, but it is a coin; losing the V from the middle leaves the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The rial is the currency of Oman, so one coin of it counts as a small Omani piece of money.

clue.text: Shut school to contain onset of lice and, later, that of scabies

indicators.note: the onset of something is its start, so only the first letter is kept
this repeats the earlier request for a word's opening letter
to contain is to hold within, so letters go inside the outer word

blocks.note: a coed is a coeducational school, taking boys and girls
first letter
first letter

explanation.surface: A school closes its doors after an outbreak of head lice followed by scabies.
explanation.walkthrough: The two initials go in separately: the first near the front, the second 'later', one letter further along. A coed is a US-style mixed school.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut and closed are synonyms describing something, like a door or a school, that is no longer open.

clue.text: Flyer emptied fuel etc mostly below field

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving only its outer letters
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
in a down entry, what is below is written after the other piece

blocks.note: a lea is a meadow in poetic usage
first and last letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pilot runs out of fuel and supplies and comes down in a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' suggests an aviator, but it means a printed handout; in this down entry LEA sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A flyer is a single printed sheet handed out for advertising, which is exactly what a leaflet is.

clue.text: Organ base Oscar’s broken at end of day in room

indicators.note: something broken has been split open, letting another piece in through the gap
placing one piece at the end of another means it follows after

blocks.note: SUN is the short form of Sunday
the lung is a breathing organ
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: An Oscar statuette smashes an organ's pedestal in a room at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The O breaks LUNG plus E, and that follows SUN, a common abbreviation for a day of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: A sun lounge is a glazed room in a house designed to let in plenty of sunshine.

clue.text: Thin papers rolled atop instrument

indicators.note: something rolled over is turned the other way, so its letters run backwards
in a down entry, whatever is atop comes first

blocks.note: ID is identity papers
a lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Cigarette papers rolled and left lying on top of a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thin' works as a verb here, meaning to weaken a liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: To thin a sauce or paint is to weaken it by adding water, which is what it means to dilute.

clue.text: After five, Enid unhappily settles for local tipple

indicators.note: unhappy means disturbed or out of sorts, so the letters are thrown into disorder
one piece placed after another simply follows it in sequence

blocks.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
taken as written
to settle a bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: At five o'clock a grumpy Enid picks up the bill for a drink at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: VIN DE PAYS is French for 'country wine', a category of regional French wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A vin de pays is a French regional wine, so it is literally the drink of the locality.

clue.text: Check meals when king’s brought up seconds

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing letters up makes them read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: suppers are evening meals
R, short for rex, Latin for king: the letter already inside the meals that moves up
s is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: Meal portions are held back when the king has already asked for second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the king's R moves: it climbs above the E within SUPPERS, then S is added at the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or restrain it, and suppress carries that same sense of stopping.

clue.text: Invalidate yearbook having deleted the latter article

indicators.note: to delete is to strike out, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: an annual is a book published once a year
of the articles 'the' and 'a', the latter is 'a'

explanation.surface: A school yearbook is discredited after a recent piece in it was removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The latter article' reads as a later piece of writing, but it means the second of the two English articles, THE and A.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a marriage or contract is to declare it void, which is to make it invalid in law.

clue.text: Drink rebuffed by fine African herbivore

indicators.note: a rebuff sends something back where it came from, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: beer is a drink
OK means fine

explanation.surface: An African grazing animal turns down a drink, and that is quite all right.
explanation.walkthrough: The reebok is better known to many as a trainer brand, named after the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The reebok, or rhebok, is a small grey antelope of southern Africa that grazes on grass.

clue.text: Make explicit records about large thug

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the letters are written backwards

blocks.note: EPs are extended-play records
L is the abbreviation for large
a lout is a rough, aggressive man

explanation.surface: Someone puts on explicit records about a big bruiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', but it turns the records round.
explanation.definitionFit: To spell out an idea is to state it clearly and in full detail, leaving nothing implied.

clue.text: Issue framing insect part that’s tiny

indicators.note: a frame goes round a picture, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: issue means offspring, such as a son
a midge is a tiny biting insect

explanation.surface: A magazine issue shows an enlarged picture of a small part of an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a magazine number, but in the old sense of offspring it means a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgeon is a very small amount of something, a minute portion or trace.

clue.text: One who helps as main road got dilapidated

indicators.note: something dilapidated has fallen to pieces, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: the thirteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A helpful passer-by lends a hand as the main road falls into disrepair.
explanation.walkthrough: In the parable, the Good Samaritan stopped on a road to aid a mugged traveller, so the road suits the surface well.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from Jesus's parable in Luke and now names any stranger who assists someone in trouble.

clue.text: Those aboard maybe lifted plaster around vessel

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting letters makes them read from the bottom upwards
to go around something is to enclose it

blocks.note: stucco is a fine plaster for walls
a pan is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: Passengers on a ship perhaps peeled plaster off the walls around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' tempts you towards ships, but it is a kitchen pan; 'maybe' marks people on board as just one kind of occupant.
explanation.definitionFit: Occupants are the people inside a car, building or craft, and passengers aboard a vehicle are one example.

clue.text: European party roles electioneer screens

indicators.note: to screen is to shield from view, so a word lies concealed within these ones

blocks.note: the letters run on across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A campaigner vets candidates for posts in a European political party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tyrol is an Alpine region split between Austria and Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tyrolese person comes from the Tyrol in the Alps, so is a native of a European region.

clue.text: Group by fortune catching the Spanish under the radar

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so one piece is gripped inside another
by means beside, so the pieces are set next to each other

blocks.note: a clan is a family group
destiny is one's fortune or fate
el is Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A gang makes its fortune by nabbing Spaniards without drawing attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Spanish' means the Spanish word for 'the', which slips in just before the last letter of the fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something under the radar means doing it secretly, avoiding notice, which is what clandestinely conveys.

clue.text: A retired city fellow seems essentially harmless

indicators.note: retiring is withdrawing or going back, so the letters run the other way
the essence of a word is at its core, so its central letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
NY is New York
a don is a university fellow
middle letter

explanation.surface: A retired academic from the big city appears perfectly inoffensive.
explanation.walkthrough: The city and the fellow reverse together, so NY DON becomes NODYN.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodyne describes something bland and inoffensive, unlikely to provoke or upset anyone, so it is harmless.

clue.text: Silly Cindy in outfit on and off ice with no jacket

indicators.note: something on and off works intermittently, so only every other letter counts
removing a jacket strips the outer layer, so the outermost letters go and the inside stays

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth letters and so on
middle letter

explanation.surface: Foolish Cindy keeps taking her skating gear on and off, and goes on the ice without her coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outfit' belongs to the letter source, not a wordplay signal: read the even letters of 'Cindy in outfit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly and idiotic are near synonyms describing foolish, senseless behaviour or ideas.

clue.text: Rear of Oval circled by singer following Asian side

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter
to be circled is to be surrounded, so one piece lies inside the other
what follows comes after, so this piece is placed at the end

blocks.note: Edith Piaf was a French singer
last letter
f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A singer runs round the back of the Oval cricket ground after an Asian team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' does double duty in the sense that its abbreviation F is also placed last. 'Side' suggests a sports team, but it is a side dish; THE OVAL is a London cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilaff is a rice dish from Central and South Asia, often served as an accompanying dish alongside a main course.

clue.text: Unfit international male player taken back on

indicators.note: something taken back returns the way it came, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for international
M is the abbreviation for male
a prop is a front-row forward in rugby
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: An injured male international player is brought back into the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' is a rugby prop, not the obvious PRO; only the final RE is reversed. A prop is a front-row forward in rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfit in the sense of unsuitable or not appropriate matches improper, as in behaviour unfit for the occasion.

clue.text: Charlie in Sofia cycling to get turkey

indicators.note: to cycle round is to rotate, so letters from the front move to the back
one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie rides his bike around the Bulgarian capital to buy a turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: SOFIA rotates to FIASO by moving SO to the end, then C slips between S and O. 'Turkey' is not the bird or the country but a flop.
explanation.definitionFit: A turkey is slang for a complete failure, especially a show, which is what a fiasco is.

clue.text: Post delivery of food you may eat raw

indicators.note: a speaker's delivery is the way words are spoken, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: steak can be served raw as steak tartare

explanation.surface: A takeaway meal is sent through the post, food that could be eaten uncooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post delivery' reads like mail, but 'Post' is the definition and 'delivery' means speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake is a wooden post driven into the ground, for fencing or supporting a plant.

clue.text: Half-scrubbed lime beneath huge peeled alternative?

indicators.note: scrubbing half away removes half the letters, leaving the other half
peeling takes off the skin, so the outer letters go
in a down entry, the piece beneath is written after the other one

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A half-cleaned lime sits under a vast peeled one, offering a different fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: this citrus fruit could stand in for a lime. In the down entry LI goes beneath UG.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a tangelo, which could serve as a substitute for a lime in a recipe.

clue.text: Juliet moved away from sprightly family member

indicators.note: moving away from a place means leaving it, so a letter departs from the word

blocks.note: Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet
jaunty means lively and cheerful

explanation.surface: Juliet has left her lively relative behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the J off the front of JAUNTY.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunty is a parent's sister, so she is a relative within the wider family.

clue.text: Bargain acquired by one wearing smart top from Escada

indicators.note: whatever is worn goes on the outside, so one piece encloses the other
the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: neat means smart and tidy
got means acquired
I is the Roman numeral one
first letter

explanation.surface: A bargain snapped up by a woman wearing a chic top from Escada, the German fashion label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bargain' looks like a cheap buy, but here it is a verb; 'by' is part of the piece order, placing GOT I before the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To bargain is to haggle over terms, and to negotiate is to discuss terms until reaching an agreement.

clue.text: Seal almost had no fish, perhaps, by November

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: to fast is to go without food, with fish one example
November is N in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A seal nearly went without fish, perhaps until November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seal' conjures the fish-eating animal, but it is a verb meaning to close; 'perhaps' marks fish as just one kind of food.
explanation.definitionFit: To seal an envelope or container is to close it securely, and fasten carries that same sense.

clue.text: Individual tries CD reformatted back in office

indicators.note: reformatting reorganises content into a new layout, so the letters are rearranged
the back of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
last letter

explanation.surface: Someone at work tries reformatting a CD back at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: Don't confuse this with DISCREET: here the answer means separate.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means separate and distinct, so individual parts that stand apart from each other are discrete.
